companyIntro.name: Vertex Infrastructure

companyIntro.culture: Load paths, tolerances and inspection records are non-negotiable. Every assumption is checked by a second engineer.

projectBackground.name: Regional Depot Building
projectBackground.context: Progress is behind and costs are above plan. The client wants an honest forecast and a recovery plan.

manager.name: Ingrid Solberg
manager.note: Tell the client early, with numbers. Forecast, causes, recovery, and what you need from them.

assignment.title: Control the project
assignment.brief: Calculate retention, SPI, forecast at completion, apply change control, price variations in Excel and report to the client.

documents.name: Contract Terms
documents.note: Retention 4% of certified value; contract sum 12,000,000.

documents.name: Cost Report
documents.note: BAC 12,000,000; planned value 3,000,000; earned value 2,700,000; actual cost 3,375,000.

tasks.title: Retention
tasks.prompt: Retention is 4% of a certified value of 12,000,000. What is the retention amount?
tasks.reasoning: Retention protects the client until defects are fixed.
tasks.mistake: Forgetting retention overstates cash coming in.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Schedule Performance Index
tasks.prompt: Earned value is 2,700,000 and planned value 3,000,000. What is SPI?
tasks.tip: Pair it with the critical path.
tasks.mistake: SPI alone can hide critical-path delay.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Estimate at Completion
tasks.prompt: BAC is 12,000,000; EV 2,700,000; actual cost 3,375,000. Assuming the current cost performance continues, what is EAC (BAC / CPI)?
tasks.reasoning: EAC shows where cost is heading.
tasks.mistake: Reporting BAC as the forecast hides overruns.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Change Control
options: Start work on a verbal instruction
Written variation request with cost and time impact
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Variation Pricing (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Value in column D = quantity x rate.
tasks.mistake: Lump sums without build-ups get challenged.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Client Progress Report
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence progress report to the client.
tasks.modelAnswer: At month six the project is behind schedule, with an SPI of 0.90, and over cost, with a CPI of 0.80, giving a forecast of 15,000,000 against the 12,000,000 budget if nothing changes. The main drivers are late design information and ground conditions. We propose a recovery plan with added crews on the critical path and a decision on three pending variations worth 47,800. We need approval of these within seven days to protect the completion date.
tasks.reasoning: A good report gives indices, forecast, causes, plan and the client's decision needed.
tasks.mistake: Hiding bad news delays the fix.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Silent Overrun
caseStudy.background: A project reported 'on track' for eight months while CPI slid to 0.78. The client learned of a 22% overrun only at month nine.
caseStudy.challenges: Reports used planned cost, not forecast.
questions: Why did reports hide the problem?
What metric should have triggered action?
How would you tell the client?
caseStudy.solution: Vertex requires earned value reports monthly and forecast reviews with the client.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Report the forecast, not the hope.

prompts: Which index worries you more, SPI or CPI?
How do you tell a client bad news?
What would you cut to recover time?
